plan: My goal is to maximize profit. Given the "bid above your value is safe" rule and the fact that I pay the second-highest bid, I should bid aggressively to win when my value is high. Since this is the first and only round, I will bid my value plus a small increment to ensure I win if the other bids are below my value, and to potentially win if they bid just above their values. I will bid my value plus $0.10.

My goal is to maximize long-term profit. Since this is the first round and I have no historical data, I will employ a strategy that aims to win when my value is reasonably high. The "always safe to bid above your value" rule is key. I will bid slightly above my value to ensure I win if the second-highest bid is below or equal to my value, maximizing my chances of profit.

My value is $13. In a second-price auction, bidding my true value is a dominant strategy, as it maximizes my expected profit. Bidding below my value risks losing profitable opportunities, and bidding above my value risks winning at a price higher than my value (though this specific auction rule mitigates that risk somewhat by paying the second-highest bid). Given the goal is to maximize long-term profit, I will bid my true value.
